describes: How this pack's builders clad, trimmed, glazed and roofed a timber house, by the era it was built in, and what later decades put in its openings. The house assembler (tools/houses.py) reads it with the house's facts (its era, storeys, footprint, roof and dated events); the parts' functions (blender/parts/house/) have no defaults: a missing key is an error. Sizes are millimetres; a pair is a range the seed draws in. Coats are in paint.json and materials/paint-*.json, the boards' wood in materials/pine.json.

sjohus.describes: A sea house (sjøhus) on the quay: a timber-framed warehouse, its gable to the water, the loading doors stacked up the gable's middle into the face of a hoist ark (a tall gable of its own, standing out on two closed cheeks, its eave corners on the gable's rakes, its apex over the ridge), small windows either side, lapped weatherboards, clay pantiles on a boxed eave, on a course of dressed granite (wooden-town-architecture.md, sea houses; docs/references/houses/01). The type's working, whatever the era it was built in (workingOfType).

windowsByYear.note: the husmorvindu: one big pane on a pivot, easy to wash; set in a smaller opening, the old casings lost, the rest of the old hole boarded in

push.describes: How far the style pushes each working's proportions where the houses are drawn (the street's shape language, blender/resolver/eras.py STYLES at stronger; the art direction of 27 October: deep reveals, thick trims, sills and caps that throw a shadow). Factors on the working's sizes; set-backs and chamfers in millimetres. Chamfers are drawn at the near level only.

lipShade.describes: The shade a level lip (a sill, a head's cap, a drip board) throws on the face under it, pushed past what the sky alone gives so it reads at the street stop: the sky under the lip falls by shade at the lip and comes back over bandMm, along a curve of this power.

ridgeSag.describes: Old timber settles: the ridge and the eaves dip between the gables, more the older the roof's frame (the house's age, a visual reading of a fact), each roof its own share of it (seeded, claiming no history).

rainwater.describes: Zinc half-round gutters on hooks and round downpipes on clips, where the era's eaves carry a gutter: the pipe drops from an outlet near the gutter's end, by a swan neck back to the wall, to a shoe just above the ground; and the sheet metal apron dressed up a chimney's faces where it meets the covering.

notes.levels: A house's levels, each from the same facts and seed (tools/houses.py --tiers): near draws every piece; street (from 20 m) one board a run, the stones' faces without their arrises, a door's panels flat, and a box shallower than errMm its front alone; city (from 80 m) a wall's planes around its openings, the plinth one face, a window its glass and casing, a door one face. errMm is the error under a pixel at 1440p where the tier begins (0.48 mm a pixel per metre: docs/building-blocks.md, Levels).
notes.doors: Doors were paired, with square panels and an overlight, and opened inward (the research, 3. Windows and doors); a sveitser door's upper fields glazed (inf.). Sizes are this pack's assumptions, judged by look: a pair 1150-1200 wide and 2050-2150 high with its overlight, set back 70 mm in the reveal, on a threshold board 110 mm over the drip board's line; stone steps of 140-200 mm risers and 340 mm treads down to the ground. A working's door is where on the front it stands (centre, or the first bay, at the side); doorKind is which of these.
notes.sources: reviews/lt1/houses/first-pass/research-subject.md: the claddings by era (single-rebated to about 1875, double-rebated sveitser), the trims (Heng 2015: side trims 120-125 x 25, the head's drip board 30 thick at about 20 degrees standing 180 proud over the window, the sill's 120, frame to drip board about 250, brackets 480 x 125 x 50), barge boards 28-34 x 195-220 [Mandal], almost no overhang on classical roofs and a deep one with rafter ends on sveitser roofs, pantiles on battens about 30 cm apart, slate on sveitser roofs, one big chimney at mid-ridge on a classical house and two or more with corbelled crowns on a sveitser one, gutters only from the sveitser era, grey fieldstone plinths, the husmorvindu and its lost trims.
notes.exposureMm: No source gave a Stavanger board width: classical widths vary within a wall (the range is drawn per course), sveitser boards are machine-run and even. Board thickness 25-32 mm.
notes.husmor: Its size and the patch of new boards where the old, larger opening was are this pack's reading of 'openings were often made smaller' and 'the trims were usually lost' (the note's (inf.)).
notes.storeyMm: No source gave storey heights: a classical cottage's lower rooms and a sveitser house's taller ones, an assumption; the loft's floor a storey and a floor's depth over the ground floor's.
notes.marks: Where water works into the cladding, so its paint fails there first (common knowledge of painted timber, assumed; no source read: run-off under a window's sill, the boards' end grain): a sill's run-off wets the boards under it, fading over dripReachM below and dripSideM past its ends; end grain draws water a board's last endReachM. How much more the paint suffers there is the paint's (paint.json, weather).
notes.boarding: No source on how an empty house here was boarded; the archive shows the boarding fitted inside the casings, the casings and their caps left whole (docs/references/houses/09-pedersgata-81-derelict-1989.jpg, panels in the openings in 1989; 08-klinkenberggata-before-clearance-1960s.jpg, pale boards in the openings). Assumed from common practice: rough sawn formwork boards (forskalingsbord, 22 mm thick, 98-148 mm and wider when reused) stood upright in the opening between its jambs, on its sill and cut to fit under its head, setBackMm behind the casing's face, butted with uneven gaps, now and then one cut short (topGapMm) and one nailed on last over its neighbours a little out of true; held by battens nailed across their faces, one for about every spacingM of the opening's height, each a little out of level (the battens as in 09; round 4); unpainted, two nails at each end into the frame (nails: fromEndMm from the end, acrossMm either side of the board's middle). stock and sawing name the wood's record (materials/pine.json, stocks and sawings). Round 3: horizontal boards evenly spaced read as louvred shutters; round 4: boards nailed over the casing ran through its cap and sill. Round 4: with battens across them the boards stand true (outOfTrueShare 0); the battens are what sit out of level.
